initial_plan.answerability: yes: annual shares of reported motorist and cyclist deaths can be compared using crash dates and the two group-specific death-count columns
initial_plan.metric: Annual percentage of combined motorist and cyclist deaths attributable to cyclists (with the complementary motorist percentage shown)
initial_plan.denominator: For each year, all reported motorist deaths plus all reported cyclist deaths; excludes pedestrian deaths
initial_plan.population: All police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes dated 2013 through 2025; death counts from the motorist and cyclist fields

changes_after_check: No plan changes; all rows were retained, and zero death counts were kept as valid values.

data_check.facts: The population contains 2,132,218 crash rows in total; every year 2013–2025 has rows and observed dates from January 1 through December 31. Both death columns have 0 NULL and 0 negative values among the included rows. Zero values occur in 2,130,945 motorist-killed rows and 2,131,942 cyclist-killed rows overall.
data_check.decisions: Keep all in-range crashes. Retain zero death values as meaningful no-death records; exclude no rows for missing or impossible death counts. No year is flagged partial by its observed date endpoints.

limitations: The denominator includes only motorist and cyclist deaths, not pedestrian deaths or all road deaths; this is a composition comparison, not a population- or exposure-adjusted risk comparison. Date checks confirm each year has records through both endpoints but do not independently establish reporting completeness for every day.
